title: pyTooling package overrides
description: Package meta-information a package index can't answer for: licenses, the URL of a project's own LICENSE file, and repositories. Read by pyTooling.Dependency.Python.LicenseOverrides and rendered by the 'dependency-table' directive.

version.description: Structure this file is written for, checked against LicenseOverrides.SCHEMA_VERSION_LATEST. A file stating a different one is rejected rather than read on the chance that it still fits.
version.$comment: Typed as a string, and quoted in the YAML, because an unquoted 0.10 is a float and a float loses its trailing zero - so '1.10' would arrive as '1.1'.

analysedAt.description: When a human last checked these statements against the projects themselves. A package index answers for itself every time it is asked; this file is as old as whoever last looked at it.
analysedAt.$comment: The pattern is what makes this normative. 'format' is an annotation in JSON Schema and most validators - jsonschema included, unless 'rfc3339-validator' is installed - skip it, so with 'format' alone a bare date such as '2026-09-06' still validated here and then loaded as a datetime.date where the reader expects a datetime.

packages.description: A package name, optionally followed by a version expression - the shape a requirement line has. Keys are matched in the order they are written and the first one a version satisfies wins, so a narrower statement goes above the bare name it refines.
packages.$comment: May be absent, an empty mapping, or null. A file stating no packages is legal and gives no overrides, and commenting out every entry under the key leaves it with a null value - which is the shape a half-disabled file has while someone is editing it.

propertyNames.$comment: '<name>' or '<name> <expression>', where the name stops at the first character an operator can start with - so 'igraph>=0.10' splits the same way 'igraph >=0.10' does.

license.description: An SPDX license expression, such as 'BSD-3-Clause' or 'BSD-2-Clause AND GPL-3.0-or-later'.
license.$comment: Parsed by pyTooling.Licensing, so every identifier it names has to be in SPDX_INDEX - an identifier the index doesn't know is rejected here as well as in the metadata this file exists to correct.

licenseURL.description: The project's own LICENSE file. Without one, a license links to where the license itself is published - apache.org, opensource.org, spdx.org - which says what the license is but not that this project adopted it.
licenseURL.$comment: Absolute, because a rendered table links it.

repository.description: The project's repository, for a package whose 'project_urls' doesn't name one - a package pointing only at its documentation, for instance.
